_comment: Frame table for the t-59 office sample, round 24 — after consul's send-back critique (2026-08-16T20:00) named real gaps in round 23: chroma-key fringe halos on sprite edges, key-tinted speckles on the tiled wall (same root cause, multiplied by tiling), a window sprite that read as a floating monitor with a baked shadow rather than a window, a second desk that read as an unidentified device on open floor, and coarse face fidelity. Every sprite below is produced by hub/tools/rectify.py (the mandatory rectifier, t-54 engine outcome), never hand-despeckled/quantized. Re-run any manifest in rectify-manifests/ against the cited region and diff the output PNG's sha256 against the matching rectify-manifests/report-*.json (recorded when this atlas was built) to verify determinism.

round24Fixes.chromaKeyFringe: rectify.py's chroma-key was a hard single threshold: a cell was either fully background or fully foreground with its raw voted color, which is wrong for real anti-aliased edge pixels (genuine blends of foreground and background). Rebuilt as a soft two-band key: alpha ramps linearly across an inner/outer distance band, and edge-band colors are DECONTAMINATED (observed = alpha_frac*fg + (1-alpha_frac)*bg, solved for fg) instead of shipped as-is. Also found and fixed a second, subtler bug this surfaced: the shared-palette builder's bucket-averaging step (a convex combination of individually-safe votes) could itself drift back into key-adjacent territory and get handed out by snap_to_palette as if it were a safe color — this is what caused round 23's recurring magenta-tinted blotches even after raising key_tolerance. Fixed with an explicit safety filter: any palette candidate (base or accent) whose own distance to the background color falls under the outer tolerance is rejected outright, never becomes a snap target. Verified: a distance-to-background scan of every opaque and semi-opaque pixel in every round-24 sprite (idle, all 4 typing frames, wall tile, window, desk, chair) finds zero pixels within key_tolerance of the background color — zero, not 'fewer'.
round24Fixes.wallSpeckles: Same root cause as the fringe bug (the wall tile's own edge pixels), fixed by the same soft-key + palette-safety-filter change. Re-verified directly: zero key-adjacent pixels in the isolated wall-cracked.png swatch, so tiling it repeatedly across the wall band no longer multiplies stray specks.
round24Fixes.windowComposition: Dropped the disconnected 'floor light-pool' half of the window crop (scenes/scene-window-states.jpg's BLUE NIGHT cell includes a window pane AND a separate floor-light-pool graphic below it, with a visible gap between them at this sheet's own scale) — that gap plus the pool's flat parallelogram shape is exactly what read as 'a baked shadow under a floating monitor' rather than a window. window-blue-night is now JUST the window pane + frame region, repositioned higher on the wall band (away from the floor line) in office-sample.html's layout(), so there's no disconnected shape near the floor to misread.
round24Fixes.secondDeskComposition: Added a chair (props/sheet-desks-workstations-v2.jpg, row 3, the plain front-facing office chair, same sheet/light register as the desk) positioned in front of desk-tidy. An unaccompanied small rectangular object on open floor read as unidentifiable; a desk with a chair pulled up to it reads as a workstation.
round24Fixes.faceFidelity: Checked, not fixed — and explained why it's not a defect to fix. The character sprite is 20px wide at the mandated 48px-tall canonical scale (pitch is fixed by the sheet's own anchor-figure measurement, never a free parameter — 'the grid pitch is the scaling knob' per PROMPTS.md's Rectification section). At that pitch the face region is roughly 10 source-cell-widths, so facial detail resolves into a handful of blocky mode-voted cells by construction — this is the same order of coarseness any 48px-tall pixel-art character's face carries (compare any Sea of Stars party-member sprite at native scale), not a phase-alignment or vote defect specific to this pipeline. Verified the mode vote is doing its job at this pitch (checked the phase-search score for this region, unremarkable, not a bad-alignment outlier). If the boss wants a less-coarse face specifically, that requires either a bigger on-screen character scale (a scene design choice, not a rectifier fix) or a dedicated close-up face crop at a different, larger logical size (breaking the single-pitch-per-sheet rule this manifest currently follows) — flagged as an open question for the critic/boss rather than assumed away.

rectifyManifests: rectify-manifests/ (one JSON per sheet; pitch is derived per-sheet from that sheet's own 48px anchor figure, never guessed or shared across sheets)

sourceSheets.idle-0: cast/sheet-agent-undercut-typing.jpg, column 0 (the anchor figure) of the 5x2 grid, row 1. HONEST FLAG (unchanged from round 21-23): this is the standing-away-from-desk pose reused as 'idle', not a true seated-idle pose — no sheet in the current set shows the character idle AT the desk without typing (kit prompt 28, 'seated idle', is still open per PROMPTS.md's NEXT WINDOW list).
sourceSheets.typing-0..3: cast/sheet-agent-undercut-typing.jpg, row 1, columns 1-4 of the same 5x2 grid — the character's own integrated desk/monitor/lamp, one continuous piece of source art, same light register as idle-0 by construction (same sheet, same row).
sourceSheets.wall-cracked: props/sheet-tiles-surfaces-v2.jpg, row 1 column 4 (cracked plaster wall texture) — picked over the sheet's warmer wood-tone wall option for the cool spy-HQ register.
sourceSheets.desk-tidy: props/sheet-desks-workstations-v2.jpg, row 2 column 3 (a plain desk already dressed with a folder + keyboard in the source art) — a SEPARATE desk from the character's own seat, not a merge onto it (see layoutNote).
sourceSheets.chair: props/sheet-desks-workstations-v2.jpg, row 3, the plain front-facing office chair — same sheet as desk-tidy, added this round for composition context.
sourceSheets.window-blue-night: scenes/scene-window-states.jpg, row 2 column 1, labeled BLUE NIGHT — window pane + frame ONLY this round (the floor-light-pool half of that cell was dropped, see round24Fixes.windowComposition).

layoutNote: The mission's re-scope names sheet-desks-workstations-v2 as the desk source, but the typing sheet's character is already drawn integrated with its own desk/monitor/lamp (one inseparable piece of source art). Rather than attempt a pixel-level merge of two different sheets' desks under one seated figure — the two-light-sources mechanical-floor violation that sent round 20 back — this round sources BOTH: the character keeps its own integrated desk (typing-0..3), and a second, separately-extracted desk (now with a chair) sits elsewhere in the corner as additional furniture. Flagged as an open interpretation call, not assumed silently; a future round can revisit if the boss reads the mission text more literally.

droppedThisRound.standalone-folder-crop: Attempted (round 23) a second, standalone folder crop from props/sheet-desk-supplies-v2.jpg — came back as a near-solid tan block, a bad region fit. Dropped; desk-tidy's own built-in folder covers the 'dressed desk' ask on its own. Not retried this round (composition/chroma-key fixes took priority).
